key_idea: Light i is green at integer time t iff t mod (r+g) >= r; simulate t, jumping straight to the next green start of any light that is red.
sketch: All lights are synchronised at t=0, so the condition is t mod p_i >= r_i with p_i=r_i+g_i. Note t = lcm(p_i)-1 always satisfies it, so -1 never actually occurs and the answer is below lcm(2..20) ~ 2.3e8. Loop on t: find the first light that is red and advance t by r_i - (t mod p_i); if none is red, print t. Lights are ordered by smallest green fraction so reds are found quickly and jumps are long; adversarial g=1 cases ran in about 30 ms. Stress-tested against a naive per-second simulation. Pitfall: use 64-bit and do not step one second at a time across all ten lights without jumping.
